Disappointing and loud experience with so-so meat
Feb 2026 • Family
OKu Restaurant left me pretty disappointed, mainly because the wagyu was the reason I came. The slices were cut so thin that there was barely any texture or “meatiness” to enjoy, and whatever flavour was there got completely ovewhelmed under the accompanying sauces. The sauces were so overpowering that instead of enhancing the wagyu, they became the main event — which defeats the whole purpose of ordering wagyu in the first place.

Another issue is the menu itself: it feels stale, like it hasn’t been refreshed or evolved in a long time. (This is our seventh visit to the hotel). On top of that, the “seafood + steaks” approach ends up diluting the experience rather than expanding it. Instead of offering real depth in either direction (a truly standout steak program or a thoughtfully curated seafood selection), the combination makes it feel like neither side gets the focus it needs. The result is a menu that’s broad on paper but doesn’t deliver a distinctive or memorable identity.

Lastly - the ambience. loud, party music didnt feel appropriate for the experience that should be savoured...

If OKu wants to lean into premium meat, I’d love to see thicker cuts and lighter, more balanced sauces, plus a menu update that brings more intention and variety. As it stands, it didn’t justify the expectation that comes with wagyu.

Fine Dining? Only if Olive Garden is Tuscany
Sep 2025 • Solo
If Olive Garden still defines “authentic Italian” for you, then OKU at Regent Phu Quoc will feel like the height of fine dining. For the rest of us, it’s theatre disguised as gastronomy.

The head chef, clearly under orders to deliver “an experience,” spends much of the evening moving from table to table. It’s more cruise ship entertainment than culinary leadership. The sommelier, just barely of drinking age, passionately extols Riesling as though he personally discovered it last week.

The ambiance? Think train station concourse moodily dimmed, with IKEA-catalog furniture that neither matches nor complements. The music is loud, the lighting impractical, the acoustics echoey. A single candle flickers bravely, but without much success.

As for the tasting menu: plenty of drama, little depth. More noise than nuance—ultimately, much ado about not much.

WOW WOW WOW
Nov 2024 • Couples
My wife and I had the 6 course signature dinner and it was sensational.

The restaurant ambience is equal to if not better than any fine dining decor that I have experienced around the World.

The staff are very knowledgeable and attentive, but you also feel that you have your own private dining experience as they are never intrusive.

The flavours were of a different level and the amount of food was perfect as we left feeling very satisfied but not completely full and bloated.

The kitchen is fully open so you can witness the artistry of the chefs as they go about creating their masterpiece dishes and it is very intriguing to watch how they strive for perfection which is a skill all on its own.

The Head Chef even took time to visit our table to enquire about our experience and thoughts on the dishes him and his team served which was a very nice touch

Would highly recommend a visit to this 5 star restaurant even if you are not staying at the Regent Phu Quoc as you will not be disappointed

Order anything but the beef
Mar 2024 • Family
I had one of the strangest meals of my life here tonight. Everything was spectacular except for the one thing they absolutely had to get right. The beef was a total complete disaster. The salad, rice, cheese, fish were all made with such care and artistry. I was getting genuinely emotional as I was taken on a perfect culinary journey. Each dish more impressive than the last. Then came the beef. Probably one of the worst cuts of meat I have ever been served in my life. I ordered medium rare but it came out rare throughout and well done on the outside. There was no marbling. No flavor. It was like a piece of red rubber with hard fat glued to it. The beef I was served on the plane ride was better than this. Oku, you need to seriously reconsider your suppliers of beef and teach your staff how to cook it properly.
